sections.heading: Render limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Starter web list price is compute — Pro list price is the production workspace floor; Not managed WordPress hosting (WP Engine) — landscape only; Not a hosting control-panel licence (Plesk/cPanel) because it forces process changes or add-ons around Render when infrastructure monitoring is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Hobby until infrastructure monitoring is mandatory; plan jumps to Starter web service only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain infrastructure monitoring at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Hobby · free · infrastructure monitoring | Starter web service | Pro.

Alternative context: unlike Fly.io, Render is preferable when Teams that want a git-push app platform with a published Pro list price production floor because infrastructure monitoring plus infrastructure monitoring match; prefer Fly.io when Teams buying managed WordPress (WP Engine) or managed VMs (Cloudways) — landscape only because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Render
sections.body:
Scenario: for infrastructure monitoring teams, recommend Render when Teams that want a git-push app platform with a published Pro list price production floor; recommend an alternative path when Teams buying managed WordPress (WP Engine) or managed VMs (Cloudways) — landscape only because Starter web list price is compute — Pro list price is the production workspace floor dominates.

Implementation effort: setup takes a named admin for infrastructure monitoring plus a freeze window if Github are in the cutover path.

Integrations in research: Github.

Final call: proceed with Render when infrastructure monitoring plus infrastructure monitoring outweigh Starter web list price is compute — Pro list price is the production workspace floor; walk when Teams buying managed WordPress (WP Engine) or managed VMs (Cloudways) — landscape only because workarounds will eat the Starter web service spend.
